_meta.about: CSS selectors for LinkedIn profile sections. LinkedIn's HTML is brittle — these may break on any DOM change. Prefer data-* attributes and semantic classes if LinkedIn adds them.
_meta.parsing:
Each selector returns a list of elements. Text is extracted,
replaced with newlines, .visually-hidden stripped. The processer iterates by index across keys (basic[i] -> description[i]).

main.name: h1
main.description: div > div.scaffold-layout.scaffold-layout--breakpoint-xl.scaffold-layout--main-aside.scaffold-layout--reflow.pv-profile.pvs-loader-wrapper__shimmer--animate > div > div > main > section > div.ph5 > div.mt2.relative > div:nth-child(1) > div.text-body-medium.break-words
main.main_skills: div > div.scaffold-layout.scaffold-layout--breakpoint-xl.scaffold-layout--main-aside.scaffold-layout--reflow.pv-profile.pvs-loader-wrapper__shimmer--animate > div > div > main > section:nth-child(4) > div:nth-child(4) > div > ul > li > div > div > div.display-flex.flex-column.align-self-center.flex-grow-1 > div > div > div:nth-child(2)

about._about: Acerca de / About section. Source overridden to main.html via source_override in processer.py, same as volunteering. The layout that actually runs today (post-2025 React/SDUI) is handled by _extract_new_layout('about', ...) in processer.py, which anchors on the componentkey ending in 'About' rather than this CSS selector — this entry exists mostly so markdownify() knows to call that path at all (it iterates this file's keys) and to document/fall back for the legacy layout, which has not been observed live.

featured._about: Featured posts/sections on the profile. Falls back to empty list if none.
featured.title: .pv-profile-component-builder__card [class*="inline-show-more-text"]

experience._about: Returns a mix of company headers (3 items: name, type, location) and role entries (2 items: title, dates). _enrich_experience() in processer.py groups roles under their preceding company header by item count.
experience._alternatives: Could use aria-level or role attributes if LinkedIn adds them. Currently no data-* attribute distinguishes headers from items.
experience.description: div > div > div.display-flex.flex-column.align-self-center.flex-grow-1 > div > ul > li:nth-child(1) > div > ul > li > div

education._about: Both basic and description use the same selector. basic extracts [institution, degree, dates]. description should target sub-components but shares same element — may need separate selector if LinkedIn adds nested detail text.

certifications._about: License certifications. basic = [title, issuer, id], dates = issue/expiry date, description = optional sub-details.

projects._about: Projects section. basic = [project_name, association], description = details, skills = associated tech stack.
projects.basic: div > div > div.display-flex.flex-column.align-self-center.flex-grow-1 > div.display-flex.flex-row.justify-space-between > div > div > div > div

volunteering._about: Volunteering section. Source overridden to main.html via source_override in processer.py. basic = [org, role, dates, cause].
